title: Vazquez’s sacrifice exception (protestation of omnipotence) would ban every relative latria-act toward images
source_text: XLIII. Vazquez quidem, cum aliis Scholasticis, rationem aliquam affert, cur imagines sacrificiis coli, ne quidem per accidens, aut relative possint; nempe, quia in sacrificiis Protestatio quaedam est divinae omnipotentiae & dominationis. Verum si haec ratio bona est, ut revera est, inde quoque sequitur reliquos Latriae actus, ne quidem relative sive concomitanter, imaginibus exhiberi posse. Nec enim ullus Latriae actus est, in quo non includatur agnitio & Protestatio virtutis cujusdam & excellentiae divinae, absque quo Latriae actus dici non posset. In hoc enim, juxta Scholae Romanae usum, Latria differt a Dulia, Quod Dulia sit honor qui debetur excellentiae creatae; Latria vero honor qui debetur excellentiae increatae. Quod si agnitio divinae alicujus excellentiae, quae est in caeteris Latriae actibus, non obstat quin imaginibus relative exhiberi possint, cur obstabit, quae est in sacrificiis, Omnipotentiae & Dominationis divinae protestatio?
pass_a_gloss: Vazquez indeed, with other Scholastics, brings some reason why images cannot be cultivated by sacrifices, not even per accidents, or relatively; namely, because in sacrifices there is a certain Protestation of divine omnipotence and dominion. But if this reason is good, as it truly is, thence it also follows that the remaining acts of Latria cannot be exhibited to images, not even relatively or concomitantly. For there is no act of Latria in which there is not included an acknowledgment and Protestation of some divine virtue and excellence, without which it could not be called an act of Latria. For in this, according to the usage of the Roman School, Latria differs from Dulia, That Dulia is the honor which is due to created excellence; but Latria the honor which is due to uncreated excellence. But if the acknowledgment of some divine excellence, which is in the remaining acts of Latria, does not hinder that they can be relatively exhibited to images, why will the protestation of divine Omnipotence and Dominion, which is in sacrifices, hinder?
pass_b_english: Vazquez fences sacrifice off because it protests omnipotence and dominion.
But every latria-act protests some uncreated excellence—so the fence would outlaw all relative image-latria, not sacrifice alone.

lemmas.gloss: a Protestation of omnipotence and dominion

choices.why: School definition hinged on uncreated vs created excellence.
